content: In an incident amid heightened tensions, a Russian SU-27 fighter aggressively approached a US RC-135U intelligence-gathering plane during its routine flight in international airspace over the Sea of Okhotsk, demonstrating its armament, leading to discussions between defense officials.

Prince Charles and Camilla will embark on a 12-day royal tour visiting 12 towns and cities in Australia and New Zealand, including a birthday barbecue in Western Australia for the 67-year-old heir to the British throne, during which they will also meet the newly appointed Australian Prime Minister Malcolm Turnbull.
A 70-something woman attacked in Sneem, County Kerry on September 20th has led to the detention of a suspect found in Killarney and being questioned by police.

Former GP Hugh McGoldrick's name will be erased from the medical register after failing to appeal against the Medical Practitioners Tribunal's decision to erase his name, following his admission of falsifying drug trials on sleep disorder patients.

A body was found in a wooded area near Dorking, and a 21-year-old man has been arrested on suspicion of murder, with additional questioning allowed as police await the results of a post-mortem examination.
Josh Hanson, a man from north-west London, died after being stabbed in the neck at the RE bar in Eastcote, Hillingdon, and police are seeking witnesses from the night of the incident.
Hovertravel is considering a potential cross-Solent ferry service between Sandown on the Isle of Wight and Southsea, operating twice weekly during July and August, if approved, to boost tourism.

In the early hours of Sunday, a person was attacked by multiple individuals in the Heights area, leading to the arrest and subsequent release on bail of a 30-year-old man, with police now seeking additional information about the incident.

As monsoon rains continue to affect millions across India, the death toll from recent floods in Gujarat has risen significantly, affecting over 450,000 people, with Prime Minister Modi planning a visit to the state to address the annual flooding issue.

Arsenal will open the Premier League's 25th season against Leicester City on a Friday night at 7:45 PM BST, as Sky Sports broadcasts the first of ten such matches in a deal that reflects the league's significant financial value and growing interest in unofficial streaming among fans.
Oldham Athletic dismissed Cristian Montano after a thorough investigation into his alleged involvement in spot-fixing, following his arrest as part of an NCA investigation.

A 20-year-old man named Rick Edwards has been sentenced to a suspended prison term and supervised probation after admitting to starting a fire at the former Pontins resort in Brixham that caused significant damage to the site.

Former Celtic player Wilson, aged 30, returned to Nottingham Forest in 2013 for £2.5m but was released in May, having played 51 games for the club across two stints, and now finds himself without a team.
Australian bowler Jack Faulkner took a hat-trick to dismiss three consecutive Sri Lankan batsmen, helping Australia secure an 82-run victory and level the five-match series at 1-1.

Sale's 32-year-old Moldovan international forward Vadim Cobilas will leave the club to join French Top 14 side Bordeaux, while the team is also considering offers for several other players whose contracts are expiring.

India's dominant start to the match, including centuries from Shikhar Dhawan and Virat Kohli, was followed by a dramatic collapse, allowing Australia to secure a narrow victory and maintain their perfect series record against India.

Safety concerns over potential debris from a large fire led to the suspension of parts of the Hammersmith and City and Circle Lines in London, with the London Fire Brigade requesting the temporary closure.
Jamie Hamill, a 27-year-old player with a background at Kilmarnock and Hearts, is returning to Rugby Park after signing a three-year contract, marking his 150th appearance for the club.
While celebrating Paul Anderson's goal, Ipswich fan Ross Morgan accidentally punched a hole through his ceiling with a celebratory fist pump, leading Anderson to offer to pay for the repairs.

Retailers in Wales must now keep cigarettes out of public view unless requested by a customer, with non-compliance potentially leading to significant fines and imprisonment, and public health officials supporting the move as a way to reduce smoking's appeal.

Wood's Luke Garrard believes that Lucas, who has previously scored three goals in 10 appearances for the National League side and made his debut for Bristol Rovers in 2014, will provide attacking depth and goal-scoring threats to the squad.

Network Rail is undertaking renovations at Knaresborough station, including making it watertight, removing and rebuilding the signal box chimney, and working on the platform canopy at night to reduce disruption, while train operator Northern notes the station's historical significance.

Lawrence Phillips, a former NFL star who struggled with legal troubles and personal demons, was found dead in his prison cell, with enough evidence emerging to potentially try him in the death of his former cellmate.

The Northern Ireland Transport Minister has proposed extending bus lane operating hours for the Belfast Rapid Transit system to 12 hours a day, from 07:00 to 19:00, with plans for community consultation to refine the details.

Lionel Messi scored his 287th La Liga goal for Barcelona to extend his lead as the competition's all-time top scorer, securing a victory against Atletico despite starting on the bench and overcoming an early goal deficit.

Italian authorities have arrested over 30 individuals, including players, directors, and potentially a police officer, from lower division football clubs in an investigation into alleged match-fixing organized by the 'Ndrangheta mafia syndicate.

Natural England and Suffolk Wildlife Trust, with support from the BBC Wildlife Fund, released 1,600 hybrid Dolomedes plantarius spiderlings into dykes at Castle Marshes between Lowestoft and Beccles to increase genetic variability and enhance adaptation to local conditions and climate change.
The Partition of India in 1947 led to the independence of two new countries and resulted in the displacement of millions of people who became refugees.

Iva Barr, a seasoned marathon runner, completed 14 miles of the London Marathon before finishing the remainder by train and walk, reflecting that despite not finishing, she had a memorable and positive experience.

In China's top cities, where property demand is extremely high and the market is unaffordable, some couples are resorting to fake divorces to purchase additional homes, despite efforts by the central bank to control prices and address the issue for low-wage earners.

A 24-year-old man was arrested on suspicion of murder after a landlord named Mr. Jones died following a stand-off with police on the roof of a pub in Holyhead, and officers are seeking witnesses from a bus that passed through the area during the incident.
The article provides instructions for following BBC News Entertainment on social media platforms and suggests emailing for story suggestions.

In a collision near Carsphairn, two men from Ayrshire, a 46-year-old van driver and a 50-year-old car driver, died after the van driver's vehicle struck the car head-on; police are seeking information from witnesses, particularly those who saw a white flatbed pickup truck in the area at the time of the crash.

Sarah Tait, an Australian rower who won a silver medal and battled cervical cancer, was praised as an inspirational role model and friend by those who knew her, including Olympic teammate Helen Glover.

In Kabul, two suicide bombings targeting military buses have injured several people and killed at least 15 others, occurring as Afghanistan and the US signed a deal allowing continued US troop presence post-2014, with Taliban claiming responsibility for the attacks.

Daimler reported strong growth in car and truck sales, predicting full-year sales exceeding 100 billion euros, despite slowing sales in China, and maintaining confidence in future growth in emerging markets.

A lifeguard rescued the 10-year-old son of Crown Prince Frederik from a dangerous rip current on the Gold Coast, potentially saving his life, though Danish officials later played down the severity of the incident.
An elderly man's body was found inside his home during a fire in Elgin Road, Elgin, with no suspicious circumstances initially suspected by police.

Veterans with amputation-related medical complications can now receive specialized treatment at the Defence Medical Rehabilitation Centre in Surrey, mirroring a tertiary referral system within the NHS and ensuring they have access to advanced care for their complex traumas.
Four speed enforcement cameras on a Welsh section of the M4 have significantly reduced the number of drivers caught speeding compared to a previous trial period, according to local authorities.

A teacher from Manchester, arrested in Spain, is suspected of taking secret photos of his students and sharing sexually explicit images of minors, including those of a particular girl, via cloud storage services and email.
A sturgeon named Steve, valued at up to £1,000, escaped from a shopping center during floods and was found in a puddle near a car wash, though he suffered minor injuries but is otherwise doing well.

Comedian Chris Rock, who has been married to Malaak Compton-Rock for 19 years, has filed for divorce while requesting privacy as they work through the process with their two daughters, Lola Simone and Zahra Savannah.
A collision occurred on the motorway between junctions 13 and 14 near Tamnamore, causing closures and traffic disruptions, with police requesting witnesses to come forward.

The Vatican's failure to respond to France's nomination of Laurent Stefanini as its ambassador within the usual six-week period suggests a potential rejection, which could be interpreted as a disagreement with Pope Francis's more liberal stance on homosexuality.

The Nasdaq experienced its largest one-day fall since April 2014, closing down 2.4%, despite a significant rise in Kraft Foods' shares following its merger agreement with Heinz, while other sectors like semiconductors and biotech saw sharp declines.

Czech player Anna Vondrousova defeated Estonian Anett Kontaveit to advance in the tournament and move closer to the top 100 ranking, while Croatia's Borna Coric won his first ATP title by saving match points against Philipp Kohlschreiber in the final.

Stoke City have signed Cameroon forward Eric Choupo-Moting, who they had previously attempted to bring to the club four years ago, as their fourth summer signing ahead of the upcoming Premier League season.

A 56-year-old man with cerebral palsy who died at a Maine private nursing home last September was finally treated as a murder victim after an autopsy in April, with police questioning a woman at Antrim PSNI station regarding the case.

Heavy rains triggered by a depression in the Bay of Bengal have caused widespread flooding, leading to the closure of many institutions and the displacement of thousands in Chennai and neighboring regions of Sri Lanka.
A bus caught fire near Largs, Scotland, but the driver efficiently evacuated the passengers, ensuring no one was injured as the emergency services attended to the situation.

Notts' Jake Ball, after a fit and fitter winter, is leading the bowling attack with Stuart Broad, demonstrating impressive form in the County Championship with six wickets in each of the team's first two games, despite a recent loss to Lancashire.

An estimated 120 "Jersey Pals" were among the 863 men who died during the Battle of the Somme, and their sacrifice is commemorated by a memorial stone made from Jersey granite, unveiled in France and featuring a core that will return to Jersey to become part of a monument in Royal Square.
Acting alum and Star Wars star John Boyega, now a member of Theatre Peckham, returns to give back to the theatre that supported him as a child while promoting his upcoming film work.

Thailand's Aphibarnrat and England's Andy Fitzpatrick are tied for the lead at 12 under par after a strong performance from Fitzpatrick, while other notable players like Luke Donald and Lee Westwood are close behind.

Middlesex gained a significant advantage with a strong third-wicket partnership of 279 runs between Voges and Malan, leaving the team in a strong position to secure their first County Championship win of the season against Hampshire.

A 52-year-old woman died and a 16-year-old boy remains critically injured after a tragic incident in Penilee Road, with police seeking to interview a 54-year-old man connected to the case, who has since been located in the Dumfries and Galloway area.

The former childhood home of a Beatle, located on Newcastle Road in Wavertree, sold at auction to an anonymous bidder after a competitive bidding process, despite a guide price of between £150,000 and £250,000.
Aaron Joseph, who faces a trial for denying owning a dog that injured David Ellam, whose death prompted the case, had previously pleaded guilty to possession of cannabis.

Thomas Bebbington, a 22-year-old from Shrewsbury, was last seen entering a river near Dana Steps on November 10th and was found dead in a body discovered by a member of the public about 10 miles away from Shrewsbury on Monday.

Five-week-old otters born in captivity are thriving but still require frequent feedings and will not be able to survive on their own until summer, when they will move to a larger outdoor enclosure with a pool and live food.

A 33-year-old woman named Joanne Thompson, a mother of four, was discovered at her home in Newtownards on Wednesday, and police are seeking witnesses to a potential disturbance at a nearby bonfire and any unusual activity near her home the previous night.

This spring, nearly 2,300 black-tailed godwits made a significant stopover on the Scottish island of Tiree, more than doubling the previous record, with many birds reportedly originating from continental Europe.

Rangers' long-serving coach Paul Durrant, who has had various roles with the club since 2005, is being let go by new manager Mark Warburton, who aims to change the coaching staff for the upcoming season.
An albino deer, a rare occurrence estimated to happen once every 100,000 births, has attracted much attention from visitors.

Asad Khan, a student from Bradford who died three weeks after starting at Beckfoot Upper Heaton School, was reportedly experiencing bullying, according to his family, who maintain he felt unsafe and planned to skip school; an inquest is considering whether to call the alleged bully as a witness.

A mysterious 17th-century painting of Charles II's 1654 coronation ceremony, believed to have been in Rokeby Park since at least 1880, remains a puzzle regarding its origin and valuation despite recent restoration and expert examination.
Macclesfield Town defeated Wrexham 3-0, lifting themselves to seventh place in the table and leaving Wrexham in 15th.

Total has become the headline sponsor of the Confederation of African Football (CAF) and its 10 competitions, taking over from Orange for the 2017 Africa Cup of Nations and beyond, though the financial details of the deal have not been disclosed.

The new Spain national team squad under coach Luis Enrique includes experienced players like Fabregas and Pedro alongside younger talents, preparing for upcoming friendlies against Belgium and Liechtenstein as part of their World Cup qualifiers.

A large, deliberate wildfire has broken out in an area spanning five kilometers and involving multiple jurisdictions, prompting an extensive response from firefighters and raising concerns about potential arsonists continuing their reckless behavior.

After a two-year hiatus from international cricket, Stuart Rankin, a former England cricketer who switched allegiance to Ireland in 2012, is returning to represent his home nation, Ireland, in time for the upcoming World Twenty20 and Test status bid.

The Northern Ireland Rare Disease Partnership, formed with the Patient Client Council, seeks to improve treatment and care for those affected by rare diseases through advocacy, education, and provision of special services, as exemplified by Jane Stewart's hope it will better support families like hers dealing with Spondylo Ephysial Dysplasia.

Gloucester Cathedral is expanding its choir to include girls for the first time, aiming to discover talented young singers from diverse backgrounds and ensuring both genders will continue to contribute to the cathedral's musical worship for years to come.

Chelsea's 29-year-old winger Pedro was taken to the hospital after suffering an injury during a 3-0 win in Beijing, although he later posted that everything was OK and will wear a protective mask upon returning to training, while the rest of the squad continues their tour in Singapore.

Nottinghamshire has hired James Taylor and former captain Paul Sales to provide cricketing guidance and technical advice to the team's batsmen, with Taylor focusing on one-day cricket experiences and Sales offering broader batman expertise.

A man has been charged with multiple offenses, including criminal damage and assault on police, after an incident witnessed by prescription pickup patients, including children, on Whiterock Road in Belfast on Friday afternoon.
When the vessel's engine failed, a volunteer crew from the Larne RNLI successfully used both their inshore and all-weather lifeboats to tow the distressed yacht to safety in Carrick Marina.
The article describes a closely contested football match between Ipswich and MK Dons, ending with Ipswich winning 3-2, while the managers discuss the season's highs and lows.

A motorcyclist suffered broken ribs when a bridge collapsed onto the M25 motorway near junctions four and three, prompting the issuance of summons for the driver involved, who faces multiple charges including dangerous driving and criminal damage.
A flashmob in Platja d'Aro, organized as a paparazzi simulation, led to a panic and stampede among holidaymakers, resulting in injuries and arrests of the participants.

Two-and-a-half-year-old Jeremiah Regis, found with over 100 injuries including a fatal bite to the chest, died after being attacked by his mother Sindyann Regis and stepfather Chevaze Mcgregor, who have been charged with his murder.

A large gorse fire on Woodbury Common, fueled by high winds, has prompted the deployment of twenty fire engine crews, a police helicopter, and has resulted in several injuries and evacuations, with firefighting efforts expected to continue through the night.

The British Speedway Promoters' Association and Leicester Speedway have reached an agreement and signed a 15-year lease for the Beaumont Park venue, marking what is hoped to be a new start for the club with a promising future.

Charles Gordon, 51, appeared in court facing a charge of murder in relation to the death of his sister Elizabeth Bowe, 50, after she was found injured at her home in St Andrews and later died in hospital.

Jim O'Brien, a 29-year-old experienced midfielder with a history of playing for clubs like Celtic and Motherwell, has signed a two-year contract with Ross County after a successful loan spell last season, bolstering the team ahead of the new campaign under manager Jim McIntyre.
Northants secured a significant lead over Durham by dismissing key batsmen early in Durham's innings and then limiting further damage in their own, despite losing wickets themselves.
New Zealand's Lydia Ko is one shot behind the joint leaders after two rounds of the LPGA Championship, with only five players under par at the halfway stage.
Former footballer and coach Alan Watson has accepted a role as assistant to Scotland's national team manager Gordon Strachan, working alongside Mark McGhee.

Belfast Giants secured a 6-2 victory over Braehead Clan, with key goals from Colin Shields, Ryan Martinelli, Mark Garside, Alex Foster, and Steve Saviano, while Scott Aarssen scored a consolation goal for the Clan.

Defending champion Jordan Spieth suffered a shocking collapse, dropping a quadruple-bogey on the 12th hole en route to losing the Masters to Danny Willett, marking a significant turning point in his career according to fellow champion Nick Faldo.
The BBC invites people to share their photos through various platforms, providing guidelines on submission and usage rights while emphasizing safety precautions.

The prosecution argues that an optometrist failed to detect signs of a potentially fatal condition during a routine eye test, leading to the death of Vincent Barker, and they contend her conduct was criminally negligent.

Food price inflation in China rose to 4.9% in June from 3.2% in May, partly due to increasing pork prices, exceeding expectations but remaining below the government's target, and likely to keep monetary policy neutral in the face of global economic uncertainty and concerns over property bubbles.

The memorial service for footballer Yaya Touré Tiote, who tragically died during training, was attended by friends, family, and former teammates, with tributes describing him as a brother and sharing memories of their time together.

In stage five of the cycling race, Slovakian rider Michael Sagan won the stage and moved into second overall, with Colombian Nairo Quintana maintaining the lead as the Tour continues with two stages remaining.

Cuadrilla's fracking project at Preston New Road in Lancashire was approved despite ongoing legal challenges, with the company promising to invest in the local economy through job creation and community initiatives.

Three teenage boys from north-west London were arrested upon returning to the UK after attempting to travel to Syria, weeks after three schoolgirls from east London had been found traveling to Istanbul with the same intention.

A respiratory consultant at the Royal Berkshire Hospital highlighted what he perceived as excessive pricing for a blackout blind, suggesting that the hospital's budget allocation may be misused despite claims of inadequate funding.

Swansea City's youth team achieved significant success with a cup final victory and 31 wins across all competitions during the 2016-17 season, contrasting with the senior team's narrow escape from relegation.

Following severe storms in December 2013 that damaged the dune system at Barkby Beach in Prestatyn, Denbighshire councillors are considering creating a secondary dune system to mitigate flood risks, which were exacerbated during the previous winter's extreme weather events.

South Shields, an eighth-tier football club captained by Julio Arca, will host an FA Cup tie against Bridlington Town on August 19th, with the match available for live streaming and on-demand viewing across various BBC platforms, and fans can interact with the commentary team via social media.

Police in Scotland are investigating what they believe to be a targeted attack, during which a 38-year-old man sustained serious facial injuries while a 49-year-old was left unharmed, and are appealing for witnesses or information about suspicious activity in the area.
Pamela McLaggan pleaded guilty to manslaughter instead of murder following the death of Jonathan Baines, who was found dead at a house in Gainsborough on August 1st.

A 15-year-old boy was attacked by a man and woman in their 40s at Patterton station, suffering facial injuries and having his mobile phone stolen, after an altercation involving a group of younger boys and older people on a train earlier that night.

A Dewsbury teenager was questioned under the Terrorism Act in April and bailed, while two other local teens, who were previously connected to terrorism investigations, are feared to have traveled to Syria in March to join ISIS.

The Belfast Giants have selected a largely returning roster featuring key players like Jonathan Boxill, Craig Peacock, Colin Shields, and Stephen Murphy for upcoming international hockey matches against Italy, the Netherlands, and Serbia, with the top finishers securing a spot in the 2018 Winter Games qualifying round, and there's an additional match against Italian club Cortina during the tournament.

Matthew Perry may not appear in the Friends tribute special, which will feature his former co-stars and is set to air on NBC, while he prepares to star in a new play called The End of Longing that will debut in London's West End.

Veteran midfielder Jones, who helped Burnley win the Championship last season and started their Premier League match against Swansea, is leaving the club after joining in 2013 and having a career that included stints at Manchester United and several other clubs.

Melbourne lawyer Joe Acquaro, known to the city's Italian community and who represented high-profile criminal clients, was fatally shot, with investigators suggesting potential involvement from underworld figures and noting ongoing tensions in the city's criminal underworld.

Air France Flight AF374, carrying 294 passengers from Paris to Vancouver, was diverted to Glasgow Prestwick after a slight burning smell was detected on board, landing normally and allowing for the passengers to be transferred to a second aircraft to complete their journey.

A yellow severe weather warning has been issued for parts of Wales as the remnants of Hurricane Gonzalo bring strong winds and heavy rain, with gusts exceeding 55mph inland and up to 70mph in coastal areas, potentially disrupting travel and causing surface water issues.

The article describes a visit to a children's hospital in Sheffield to explore concerns about overcrowding and its impact on patient care, including interviews with a doctor and patients like Lilly and Jake.

Kenneth David Dickie, 64, was found injured at Rockley Park in Poole and later died from his injuries, while a 34-year-old man and a 57-year-old woman have been charged or bailed in connection with the incident.

Cardiff City have retained forward Michael Macheda until the end of the season while signing midfielder David Vaughan to a one-year contract, though their pursuit of Andre Moritz was unsuccessful due to contractual issues.
The body of Christopher Huxtable was found after the building collapse in February, providing closure to his family while highlighting the ongoing search for two other missing men.

Bristol City head coach Lee Johnson emphasizes the importance of securing a victory against QPR to close the gap with other teams in the league, while noting that some of his players are either recovering from injuries or still uncertain for the match.

Italian astronaut Luca Parmitano described his experience walking in space as absolutely fantastic and expressed great excitement after completing a mission that included two spacewalks, orbiting Earth 2,656 times, and traveling over 110 million kilometers.

England Knights player Joe Arundel, who made his debut at 16 and played 44 times for Hull Kingston Rovers (referred to as "Tigers"), is excited but nervous about joining Hull FC, a move aimed at building a long-term winning culture at the club.

Ulster Bank is working to update affected payments for around 600,000 customers no later than Saturday, following an IT issue that has been fixed, though affected customers are advised to contact branches or call centers for assistance.
Tanzania defeated Kenya 2-1 in the Women's Africa Cup of Nations qualifier, while Ethiopia secured third place with a 4-1 win over Uganda in the play-off.
Due to an industrial action by dockworkers on the US west coast affecting potato supply chains, McDonald's in Japan is rationing French fries and limiting portion sizes in its restaurants.

The Classic race purse is boosted to £1.625 million with the addition of Permian and Khalidi, while trainer John Jenkins defends running 1,000-1 shot Diore Lia in the race despite her limited racing experience, citing a desire to raise funds for charity.
Atletico Madrid star Antoine Griezmann, who leads La Liga in goals for his team, will miss a match against Real Madrid and a friendly for France due to a foot injury, though no bone damage was found.

Willie Mason, a veteran prop with extensive experience in both rugby league and union, is joining the Wigan Warriors' Super League side under coach Laurent Frayssinous, aiming to bolster the team's physical presence after recent losses.

A recent survey by The Marine Conservation Society found an 11% increase in dog mess on UK beaches, with a notable 71% rise in Scotland, but also noted a decrease in overall litter levels, encouraging pet owners to use beach-provided bins for dog waste.

The Supreme Court ruled that introducing fees for employment tribunal cases was unlawful and unconstitutional, as they disproportionately affected women and prevented workers from accessing justice, leading to a significant reduction in the number of cases.
Wycombe beat Dagenham & Redbridge to climb to sixth place, despite Dagenham reducing the deficit and playing with ten men after two dismissals.

Bee-eaters, a species native to southern Europe, have successfully bred at a quarry in southern England for a second consecutive year, with all chicks having hatched and expected to fledge in the coming weeks.

A kayaker capsized in the River Wey near Guildford, and despite a rescue attempt by his son, divers are searching the area as authorities warn against entering the water due to flood warnings and the ongoing search.
A stone thrown by an elephant at a zoo in Morocco accidentally killed a girl, despite the enclosure meeting international standards, and the incident being described as rare and unpredictable.

Labour MP Sarah Glass has been appointed to the shadow cabinet despite growing calls for a leadership election, following the resignation of her predecessor Angela Powell who lost confidence in Labour leader Jeremy Corbyn.

With six teams vying for the Premier League title, including Chelsea, Manchester United, and others, Conte emphasizes the need for focus and concentration in every match as the race for the championship remains tight.
A dispersal order has been implemented in Llangefni to address anti-social behavior and alcohol-related issues by allowing authorities to remove troublemakers from the area and prevent their return.

De Roon, a 26-year-old Dutch international who scored five goals in 36 league and cup games for Middlesbrough last season, has left the club after playing 33 Premier League games, while manager Garry Monk has expressed interest in signing Chelsea midfielder Lewis Baker.

The Roald Dahl Funny Prize, a children's humor book award launched in 2008 by Michael Rosen, will be relaunched in 2016 as part of the author's centenary celebrations, with plans to strengthen its impact.

Frazier Glenn Miller Jr., a white supremacist who admitted to killing two and wounding others at Jewish facilities, was sentenced to death and executed by lethal injection after shouting "heil Hitler" in court.

The city council plans to launch a larger self-service bike scheme in April 2017, with 500 bikes available at various locations across the city, aiming to expand on a previous pilot scheme and emulate successful bike-sharing models like London's "Boris bikes."

Senegal international Diaf Sakho, who recently returned to light training after back surgery and missing much of the season, is at the beginning of a pre-season fitness regimen that could keep him out of Premier League action for some time.

The Northern Ireland residential property market showed a slowdown in price increases with an average annual rise of 5.4% in the third quarter, compared to 7% in the previous four quarters, while the number of deals remained steady at around 5,200.

A recent wind turbine part delivery in Dumfries and Galloway ended in a crash, with the lorry and cargo ending up in a ditch, contrasting with a successful previous delivery over the same route months earlier.

The Betsi Cadwaladr health board is consulting the public on potential downgrades to hospital services due to staffing shortages, amid opposition from residents who fear it would increase travel distances for maternity care.

Mignon du Preez scored a second ODI century, leading South Africa to a commanding total of 272-6 against Ireland, who were bowled out for 204, as the sides prepare for further matches on Tuesday and Thursday.

Triple jumper Peake is aiming to break her Welsh record and qualify for the Rio Olympics with a performance expected to surpass her current personal best of 4.40m at the Cardiff International Sports Stadium.

A large fire involving scrapped railway sleepers that burned for over 10 hours and was believed to be deliberately set was discovered at a building site in Bloomery Circle, Llanwern, and took crews more than 10 hours to extinguish.
A concert was held in Edinburgh to commemorate the victims of the Nepal earthquake and raise funds for relief efforts, featuring the traditional Singing Bowl Concert at St Giles' Cathedral.
Neil Lennon, Hibernian's head coach, has been banned from the technical area for the second leg of their Europa League qualifying match against Brondby due to violent conduct towards the referee.

A fire broke out in the deep-sea Boulby mine in April, causing seven workers to seek medical treatment, leading to an HSE notice being issued, and prompting the company to commit to improving safety procedures.

Two young men, one British and one French, were caught posing naked at Machu Picchu and questioned by police for offenses against morality, with no arrests or charges made, following increased surveillance at the UNESCO World Heritage site due to growing incidents of nudity.

Croatia international and Barcelona player Ivan Rakitic, who scored 23 goals in 145 appearances for Barcelona since joining from Sevilla in 2014, is set to sign a new deal with a £109m buyout clause on Friday, just days after playing a crucial part in Barcelona's Champions League comeback victory.

A couple from Halstead was kidnapped and subjected to severe violence during a home invasion in which they were threatened with the murder of their family members; police have released a description of one of the suspects and are investigating further.

The Wickerman Festival, set to take place at East Kirkcarswell Farm, will kick off with a headlining performance by Dizzee Rascal on its opening night, along with a diverse lineup featuring acts like Martha Reeves and The Vandellas, The Zombies, Big Country, and The Feeling.
Foden expresses optimism about contributing to the England rugby squad alongside his teammate Brown, as both players perform well for their respective teams in the Aviva Premiership.
A motorcyclist died after colliding with a Vauxhall Zafira car in Dagenham, while two children in the car were injured; one remains seriously injured in hospital.

Pfizer has acquired California-based Anacor Pharmaceuticals for its eczema cream crisaborole, which could potentially reach $2 billion in annual sales if approved, addressing a significant unmet medical need for millions of patients.

Police responded to a reported street fight in Dagenham, recovering multiple weapons and arresting two juveniles, while reporting no injuries and emphasizing the potential lifesaving impact of their intervention.
A 23-year-old man from Cardiff has been arrested on suspicion of sexual assault following a report of an attack on a 19-year-old woman at Gorsedd Gardens near Cardiff Civic Centre.

John Lamont's resignation from the Ettrick, Roxburgh and Berwickshire constituency leads to a multi-layered by-election where local council, Scottish Parliament, and Westminster seats will all be contested within five weeks.

Canada has lifted its ban on importing beef from the EU, including major producers like France and Germany, as part of broader trade agreements and recognizing the EU's safety measures post-BSE outbreaks, alleviating some pressure on European farmers facing export challenges.

European finance ministers have endorsed plans to create a unified EU list of tax havens and to impose sanctions on countries that do not comply, aiming to combat offshore tax evasion as part of broader efforts to crack down on hidden wealth.

Archaeological findings including pottery fragments, kilns, and Bronze Age burnt mounds were discovered during excavations for the construction of the West Link road near Torvean, providing insights into ancient practices related to heating and food preparation.
Main scored the winning goal for Oldham against Southend, securing a victory that keeps Oldham safely above the League One relegation zone while Southend remains in 13th place.

Irish actor Pádraig Lally, known for his roles in Glenroe, Ballykissangel, and The Secret of Kells, passed away peacefully after a short illness, leaving behind a legacy as a versatile performer and advocate for the Irish language.

Derby City Council has decided to keep Moorways Pool open for a year after campaigners gathered 4,000 signatures, citing savings found in other areas and a commitment to maintain the pool while planning for a new one to replace it by 2018.
UNICEF expresses concern over the detention of children in military custody after being evacuated from areas controlled by Boko Haram in northeastern Nigeria.

Hearts head coach Robbie Neilson is considering signing experienced goalkeeper Lee Hollis, who is currently a free agent, to address the team's goalkeeping situation following injuries to Alexander and Gallacher.

Chelsey Lee, a 26-year-old basketball player who won rookie of the year in the WKBL, faces lifetime suspension and record annulment after it was discovered that she and her agents fabricated her and her father's birth certificates to falsely claim she had a South Korean grandmother, leading to an investigation and changes in league rules.

An app released by Ofcom alongside its 2015 Connected Nations report indicates that while significant progress has been made in UK broadband speeds and usage, many homes still experience suboptimal wi-fi performance due to interference and lack of high-speed connectivity, especially in rural areas and among small businesses.
